claims.text: Reliable formation of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials is governed by the combined effects of elemental distribution, lattice strain, and surface defects.
Catalytic performance of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials is governed by the combined effects of elemental distribution, lattice strain, and surface defects.
Elemental distribution influences reactant adsorption and activation.
Lattice strain influences reactant adsorption and activation.
Surface defects influence reactant adsorption and activation.
Particular compositions and microstructures will provide enhanced catalytic performance and reliability relative to conventional noble metal-based catalysts.
Conventional noble metal-based catalysts used as the baseline have uniform composition and microstructure.
The proposed relationship holds within the currently synthesizable and processable range of noble metal-based high-entropy alloy compositions and microstructures.
Elemental distribution, lattice strain, and surface defects can be varied systematically through controlled synthesis and processing.
Absence of significant correlations between the three structural variables and catalytic performance would falsify the hypothesis.
